The Quantum Gardening Revolution

Can photon-powered compost save the solar system?

Zara Nova
September 1, 2099

This article was featured in the Galactic Digest newsletter. Sign up here.

In 2099, a group of Martian settlers discovered that quantum-entangled seeds could grow in zero gravity, launching a revolution in space agriculture.

Professor Orion Blackwell of the Nova Terra University published a landmark study showing that entangled radishes produced three times the yield of conventional crops.

The implications were staggering. As Blackwell wrote in The Martian Agricultural Review, the breakthrough meant that humanity could finally sustain colonies beyond Earth without constant resupply missions.

But not everyone was convinced. Critics argued that quantum gardening consumed too much energy, and the long-term effects on Martian soil remained unknown. The debate would rage for decades to come.

This article appears in the September 2099 print edition with the headline "Seeds of Tomorrow."
